hypotheses.title: Record-field annotation propagation is unmemoized: exponential on record-inclusion DAGs, quadratic on alias/inclusion chains (stage 4)
hypotheses.issue: In top-level type resolution, propagateRecordFieldAnnotations (called from resolveTopLevelAnnotationAttachments <- ResolvePublicNodes) builds a `sources` map. It has an entry for every record type definition with *inclusions and for every alias `type X Y`. For each entry it calls propagatedRecordFieldAnnotations with a fresh `visiting` map. That function recursively merges the annotations of every source (inclusion or alias target) and never caches a symbol's result, so a type reachable through many paths is recomputed once per path. A chain of N aliases/inclusions costs about N^2/2 frames. A DAG where R_i includes R_{i-1} and R_{i-2} costs about fib(N) frames. Every frame allocates a new values.FieldAnnotationValues map and calls compilerContext().RecordFieldAnnotationValues(symbol), which also allocates. The pass runs unconditionally, even when the program has no annotations. Profiling inclusion_dag_30 showed 64% of CPU in propagatedRecordFieldAnnotations and 98% of 544 MB allocated from NewFieldAnnotationValues.

reproducer.generator:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Generate a Ballerina file whose record type inclusions form a DAG
(R_i includes R_{i-1} and R_{i-2}, each overriding the shared `id` field).
propagateRecordFieldAnnotations (semantics/internal/types/type_resolver.go)
re-walks every inclusion path without memoization -> O(fib(N)) work.

usage: gen_inclusion_dag.py N [chain]   (chain => `type A_i A_{i-1}` alias chain, O(N^2))
"""
import sys
n = int(sys.argv[1])
mode = sys.argv[2] if len(sys.argv) > 2 else "dag"
out = []
if mode == "dag":
    out.append("type R0 record {| int id; |};")
    out.append("type R1 record {| *R0; int id; |};")
    for i in range(2, n):
        out.append(f"type R{i} record {{| *R{i-1}; *R{i-2}; int id; |}};")
    last = f"R{n-1}"
    out.append(f"public function main() {{\n    {last} r = {{id: 1}};\n    _ = r;\n}}")
else:
    out.append("type A0 record {| int id; |};")
    for i in range(1, n):
        out.append(f"type A{i} A{i-1};")
    out.append(f"public function main() {{\n    A{n-1} r = {{id: 1}};\n    _ = r;\n}}")
print("\n".join(out))
reproducer.command: python3 gen_inclusion_dag.py 32 > inclusion_dag_32.bal  (or: python3 gen_inclusion_dag.py 4000 chain > alias_chain_4000.bal); go build -o /tmp/bal ./cli/cmd && /tmp/bal run --stats inclusion_dag_32.bal; ./bin/benchmark --mode time --runs 5 --warmup 1 main <branch> inclusion_dag_32.bal

Scaling: DAG time grows about 2.6x per +2 records (n=24..32: 63/161/429/1143/2954 ms); alias-chain time grows about 4x per doubling (4000: 2.2 s, 8000: 9.5 s).

Wall time: -98.8% on inclusion_dag_32 (2988 -> 36 ms) and -96.9% on alias_chain_4000 (2460 -> 77 ms). Peak RSS: -9.8% on inclusion_dag_32 (40.1 -> 36.1 MiB) and -20.9% on alias_chain_4000 (67.5 -> 53.4 MiB). hypotheses.fix_approach: Within one propagateRecordFieldAnnotations call, keep memo map[model.SymbolRef]values.FieldAnnotationValues and pass it down. propagatedRecordFieldAnnotations returns the memo entry when present; otherwise it computes the merge (inherited sources minus redeclared fields, overlaid by the symbol's own field annotations) and stores it before returning. This makes the pass O(types + inclusion edges + annotations). The `visiting` set is kept for the (theoretically impossible) cycle check and can be shared across top-level calls because entries are removed on return. The result map is allocated lazily (nil when there is nothing to propagate), so annotation-free programs allocate nothing. Pitfall: cached maps are shared between callers, so they must be read-only. Both callers only read them: the recursive caller copies into its own map, and the top-level loop writes through SetRecordFieldAnnotationValue into the separate context store. The output is unchanged because a symbol's merged result depends only on its sources, its declared fields and its own annotations, and the merge order is preserved. Possible follow-ups: skip the pass entirely when the module has no record-field annotations, or process symbols in topological order.

notes: Side observation from exploration, not pursued: on corpus/bench/10-bench/default-heavy-project-v, the mutex profile shows heavy RWMutex contention on the global context/internal/functionsignatures.Store (desugar setRecordDefaultFnSignature Allocate/Associate vs stage-5 readers via functionSignatureRef). A sync.Map prototype gave no wall-time gain on 4 cores because the run is CPU-bound, so it is probably only worth revisiting on machines with more cores.
